integration_issues.issue: Tab URL sync in InvestigationDetailPage.jsx (useEffect at ~line 49-55) uses nav(..., { replace: true }) for every tab change, so switching tabs never pushes history entries. After navigating Overview → Story → Evidence → Report and pressing Back, the browser skips past the investigation page entirely (lands on '/') instead of restoring the previously viewed tab. Spec item states: 'Browser back button after tab navigation restores previous tab state without errors'. No console error is thrown; behaviour is functionally safe but does not match the described contract.

action_items: InvestigationDetailPage.jsx tab-URL sync: use { replace: true } only when initialTab is being normalized on mount; on user-initiated tab changes call nav(..., { replace: false }) (or push) so Back restores the previous tab. Recommend switching to nav(url) (push) inside a handler that fires only when tab state changes via onSelect, and keep replace-mode strictly for the initial URL normalization branch.
critical_code_review_comments: InvestigationDetailPage.jsx line 47: initialTab is computed once from location.search at mount; if a user externally changes the ?tab= param (e.g., via browser navigation) the internal `tab` state does not resync. Consider a useEffect that watches location.search and calls setTab when the parsed tab differs. This is also the same root cause of the Back-button spec miss.
The four-tab NavTabs items array is defined inline inside render each time — minor perf; consider useMemo or moving out of the component.

rca of the issue: InvestigationDetailPage.jsx useEffect at lines 49-55 calls nav(`${pathname}?${params}`, { replace: true }) on every tab state change. This unconditionally replaces the current history entry, so switching tabs never appends to browser history. Consequence: pressing Back after multiple tab clicks jumps to whichever URL preceded the investigation page (in the test, '/'), not the previously active tab. Fix: distinguish 'initial URL normalization' (should replace) from 'user tab switch' (should push). Simplest patch: wrap navigation in a check — if params.get('tab') is missing or invalid, replace; otherwise push. Alternatively, drive tab state directly from the URL query param (single source of truth) and use nav(url) without replace inside the tab-click handler.
